text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's largest Kremikovtsi steel works posted 804 million levs net profit for the first nine months and expected annual profit to total 850 million levs, the company's executive director Atanas Bogdanov said.
-- An insolvency suit against Bulgaria's state-owned Mineralbank was postponed after an anonymous bomb threat closed the court building in Sofia on Wednesday, court officials said. @
-- Bulgaria's Post and Telecommunication Committee had proposed to the cabinet to set up a Post Savings Bank, the newspaper said, quoting an unidentified government source.

-- Bulgaria's private Security Insurance Company (SIC) has posted some two billion levs income since the beginning of 1996, and the company is expected to raise its capital to 300 levs in 1997, a senior company official said. @

-- Bulgaria's president Zhelyu Zhelev has sought clarification from the International Monetary Fund on whether the Socialist government can introduce a currency board system without a political consensus.

-- Kremikovtsi steel works said it had asked the central bank (BNB) to file an insolvency suit against the illiquid Bank for Agricultural Credit because of some $3 million in Kremikovtsi's accounts stalled in the bank.

-- The European Union (EU) Commission is expected to vote on December 6 on the release of a humanitarian aid package to Bulgaria to alleviate the country's grain shortage, Bulgaria's ambassador to the EU Evgeni Ivanov said.
-- Bulgaria's biggest state Bulbank will pay principal and interest worth 2.7 billion yen to the Japanese Mitsubishibank on a 10-year bond issues due by December 2, a Bulbank official said.
-- EU inspectors arrived in Bulgaria to monitor measures to extinguish an outbreak of foot-and-mouth desease in the southeastern parts of the country. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
